## Definition  
- A blog is a website whose basic unit is a post or entry, typically presented in reverse chronological order. Blogging can be done by individuals, businesses, or organizations, and content varies widely.  

## History  
- Blogs emerged in the late 1990s, coinciding with web publishing tools that allowed non‑technical users to post content. Early blogs were often single‑author, but multi‑author blogs (MABs) grew in the 2010s, especially from media outlets, universities, and advocacy groups.  

## Features  
- Modern blogs are interactive Web 2.0 sites, allowing comments and social networking. Bloggers often moderate comments to remove hate speech or offensive content.  

## Terminology  
- The term “blog” is a truncation of “weblog”. It can also be used as a verb meaning to maintain or add content to a blog.

A **blog** (a [truncation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clipping_(morphology) "Clipping (morphology)") of " **weblog**") is a website whose basic unit is a "post" or "entry", with posts typically presented in [reverse chronological order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_chronology "Reverse chronology"). Blogging may be carried out by individuals, commercial enterprises, or organizations, and blog content varies widely.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog#cite_note-1)

In the 2000s, blogs were often the work of a single individual, occasionally of a small group, and often covered a single subject or topic. In the 2010s, multi-author blogs (MABs) emerged, featuring the writing of multiple authors, sometimes professionally edited. MABs from newspapers, other [media outlets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_media "News media"), universities, [think tanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Think_tank "Think tank"), [advocacy groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocacy_group "Advocacy group"), and similar institutions account for an increasing quantity of blog [traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_traffic "Web traffic"). The rise of Twitter and other " [microblogging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microblogging "Microblogging")" systems helps integrate MABs and single-author blogs into the news media. _Blog_ can also be used as a verb, meaning _to maintain or add content to a blog_.

The emergence and growth of blogs in the late 1990s coincided with the advent of web publishing tools that facilitated the posting of content by non-technical users who did not have much experience with [HTML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML "HTML") or [computer programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming "Computer programming"). Previously, knowledge of such technologies as HTML and [File Transfer Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_Transfer_Protocol "File Transfer Protocol") had been required to publish content on the Web, and early Web users therefore tended to be hackers and computer enthusiasts.
